newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CORDOVA THROWS SHUTOUT AS PIRATES ROUT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CORDOVA THROWS SHUTOUT AS PIRATES ROUT BRAVES.

text.p: Francisco Cordova continued his remarkable turnaround with a seven-hitter for his first career shutout and Jose Guillen homered and drove in three runs as the Pirates routed the Atlanta Braves 9-0 Friday.

Cordova (2-3), who was 4-7 with a 4.09 earned run average last season, held the defending National League champions to just five singles and a pair of doubles. He walked four and struck out a career-high eight in his first complete game.

Cordova has allowed one earned run or less in six of his seven starts and saw his ERA fall to 1.53. The Pirates scored nine runs for him against Atlanta after combining for just 12 in his first six starts.

"I'm really happy," Cordova said, "especially with the performance coming against the Braves. I hope this continues. I feel I'm pitching the same as last year. But maybe more experience lets me do more things the right way."

Guillen, who never played above Class A before this season, hit a two-run homer off starter Terrell Wade (1-2) in the fourth. Tony Womack and Al Martin added three hits apiece for the Pirates, who took two of three games from the Braves last week.
"I just tried to make contact," siad Guillen. "I feel very comfortable."
Pittsburgh has won four straight and six of eight.
Wade (1-2) was tagged for six runs -- three earned -- and seven hits in six innings.
Ryan Klesko had both doubles for Atlanta, which has scored three runs or less in each of its last eight games.
"Cordova was just too tough," said Braves manager Bobby Cox. "Wade struggled tonight and the Pirates took advantage."
At Florida, Gary Sheffield singled home Alex Arias with the winning run with one out in the bottom of the ninth inning as the Marlins edged the Houston Astros 3-2.
Errors by second baseman Craig Biggio and late defensive replacement Tim Bogar at third set up the game-winner.
Robb Nenn (2-1) tossed a scoreless ninth to pick up the win, Florida's fourth in 10 games.

Starter Kevin Brown gave up two runs over seven innings while tying a career high with 10 strikeouts, reaching the mark for the second straight start. The Marlins have produced only 11 runs in Brown's last five starts.

In Philadelphia, Calvin Maduro allowed two hits over seven innings and Rico Brogna highlighted a three-run fourth with a two-run double, leading the Phillies to a 3-1 victory over the Colorado Rockies.
Maduro (3-3), who gave up just a leadoff double in the first to Eric Young and Larry Walker's solo homer in the sixth, walked four and struck out three to avenge Sunday's 9-0 loss at Colorado.
Maduro has won all three home starts this season, allowing six runs and 16 hits over 21 2/3 innings (2.49 ERA). But he is 0-3 with an 8.20 ERA in four road starts.
In St Louis, Todd Hundley and former Cardinal Bernard Gilkey each drove in three runs as the New York Mets broke open a tight game in the late innings for a 10-3 win.
A potential go-ahead home run by the Cards' Gary Gaetti in the bottom of the sixth was ruled a double and the Mets took the lead in the seventh on Butch Huskey's fifth homer.
New York won for the ninth time in 13 games.
Mark Clark, another ex-Cardinal, won for the fourth time in five starts. He allowed three runs and seven hits in six innings with no walks and three strikeouts.
St Louis starter Todd Stottlemyre (1-2) lost to the Mets for the first time in five career decisions.
In San Diego, John Smiley gave up two runs and six hits over seven innings and matched his career high with 11 strikeouts as the Cincinnati Reds beat the Padres 7-2.
Smiley (3-5) posted his second straight win after a personal five-game losing streak. He walked none. In his last two starts, the left-hander has given up just two runs and 13 hits in 14 innings.
Smiley improved to 7-1 lifetime against the Padres.
Willie Greene, Bret Boone and Joe Oliver homered for the Reds.
In Los Angeles, Raul Mondesi and Todd Zeile hit two-run doubles in a five-run eighth inning that gave the Dodgers a 5-1 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Hollandsworth, Mondesi and Zeile had two hits apiece for the Dodgers, who won for the fourth time in their last five games.
In San Francisco, Brian McRae's one-out single in the top of the 14th inning scored Doug Glanville with the winning run as the Chicago Cubs outlasted the Giants 5-3.
McRae, Mark Grace and Ryan Sandberg hit solo homers for Chicago, which has won three of their last four games.
Bill Mueller went 3-for-6 with an RBI for the Giants, who dropped their third straight game.
